We're given that $Z∼N(0,1),$ and we wish to compute $P(-2.25<Z<2.25).$ The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14259374/assets/6d34a217c29edd92527e2c31a954af6e631755c178ecacc797ed6c0c5da0f25b.png)

By the definition of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z),$ 

$$
P(Z\le z)=Φ(z).
$$

So, we express the required probability in terms of $Φ(z)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-2.25<Z<2.25) & =P(Z<2.25)-P(Z\le -2.25) \\  & =P(Z\le 2.25)-P(Z\le -2.25) \\  & =Φ(2.25)-Φ(-2.25)\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, we know that

$$
Φ(-2.25)=0.0122,
$$

but we are not given $Φ(2.25).$ However, we can compute this using symmetry:

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(2.25) & =P(Z\le 2.25) \\  & =1-P(Z\le -2.25) \\  & =1-Φ(-2.25) \\  & =1-0.0122 \\  & =0.9878\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-2.25<Z<2.25) & =Φ(2.25)-Φ(-2.25) \\  & =0.9878-0.0122 \\  & =0.9756.\end{aligned}
$$
